E031-01.notes: Past perfect needs participle: 'had grown'. 'had grew', 'had growed', 'had grow' all ungrammatical. Facts: London ~1M in 1801, ~2.4M (1851) to 2.8M (1861), so 'well over two million' in 1858 is accurate.

E031-02.notes: Plural, non-possessive 'cesspools'; the comma closes the interrupter opened after 'flowed,' ('by way of old drains and overflowing cesspools,'). D drops the closing comma; A/C use wrong possessives.

E031-03.notes: Two independent clauses; period is correct. C comma splice, D fused sentence, B question mark makes a statement a question.

E031-04.notes: The clause explains why Parliament 'could hardly ignore the problem' - its building is on the river. A unsupported, B the chemicals detail is elsewhere and unaffected, C timing is in the next sentence. Fact: curtains soaked in chloride of lime is the commonly reported account ('reportedly' hedges it appropriately).

flags: minor: key is the shortest choice, as is typical for concision/combining items
E031-05.notes: C merges cleanly without redundancy. A/B repeat 'would carry it'; D is redundant ('Carrying... would carry'). All grammatical, so concision is the discriminator; stem 'most effectively' supports that.

E031-06.notes: 'four' is a number and 'large' is not coordinate with the noun-adjunct 'pumping'; no commas. Fact: Bazalgette's main system had four main pumping stations (Chelsea, Deptford, Abbey Mills, Crossness) - accurate.

E031-07.notes: Only B shows planning for a larger future city (tunnels sized beyond then-current needs). Historically accurate: Bazalgette famously enlarged/doubled pipe diameters for future growth. A, C, D off-claim.

flags: minor: factual nuance - Greater London today (~9 million) vs. 1858 metropolis (~2.6-2.8 million) is a bit over 3x but covers a larger area; 'more than three times' holds on standard figures
E031-08.notes: 'three times as large as' is the idiomatic comparison. B 'larger as', C 'as large than', D 'larger then' are all idiom/spelling errors.

E031-09.notes: Subject 'One' is singular, intervening 'of the original pumping stations' is a distractor; 'has been restored'. D 'were' plural. Fact: Crossness has been restored by the Crossness Engines Trust and is open for tours; its ornate Victorian cast ironwork is well known.

E031-10.notes: Paragraph 4 is the Bazalgette paragraph (count verified). B links 'planned for a city larger than the one he saw' to the present system. A and D are only about the Crossness station; C generalizes to other cities with no link to his planning.
